newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blames salmon impasse on Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blames salmon impasse on Canada.

text.p: The United States on Monday blamed the impasse in salmon talks on Canada's refusal to conserve stocks.

"Agreement has not yet been reached. We believe it is because Canada has been unable to make or accept a proposal that meets the minimum requirements to conserve salmon stocks off the West Coast," John Dinger, a State Department spokesman, told reporters.

Dinger said the United States has "made a good faith effort" to find a solution and he asserted that if Canada had not broken off negotiations in May "an agreement could have been in place right now."
With the commercial fishing season set to open as early as next week, Dinger said he was unaware that the two sides had set a specific date to resume their talks.
Canada and the United States reached a stalemate on Friday in bitter talks aimed at resolving a dispute over how to divide the Pacific salmon catch.
The two countries held three days of negotiations last week, their first meetings on the salmon dispute since talks collapsed in acrimony a month before.
